visual_identity.core_identity: An oversized predatory centipede defined by its long segmented body, one pair of legs per visible segment, and large front poison claws.
visual_identity.silhouette: Long flexible segmented body forming an S-curve or coil, with many evenly spaced legs creating a saw-tooth edge.
visual_identity.head_features: Small armored head with simple antennae and strong curved forcipule-like poison claws near the mouth.
visual_identity.body_shape: Long chain of many repeated trunk segments, with ONE PAIR of slender walking legs attached to EVERY visible trunk segment; legs form a continuous saw-tooth rhythm from immediately behind the head nearly to the tail.
visual_identity.surface: Simple armored segment plates with minimal texture.
must_avoid: sparse legs only near the head
worm body with only a few legs
visual_identity.shape_lock: Draw a long chain of many trunk segments where every visible trunk segment carries exactly one pair of short walking legs, forming a continuous saw-tooth rhythm nearly the whole body length; front mouth claws stay small and mouth-adjacent, never spiderlike or lobsterlike.
visual_identity.limb_structure: Every visible trunk segment carries exactly one pair of short walking legs, producing a continuous paired-leg rhythm from behind the head toward the tail. The head has antennae and small mouth-adjacent poison claws only; no giant pincers or spider legs.

accuracy_checks: body is not mistaken for snake
every visible trunk segment carries one pair of legs
continuous repeating leg rhythm runs along nearly the entire body
front poison claws stay small mouth-adjacent forcipules, not giant pincers

reference.notes: Reference material controls creature identity, anatomy, and silhouette only; Black-Ink controls the final coloring-book rendering style.

description: An oversized predatory centipede defined by its long segmented body, one pair of legs per visible segment, and large front poison claws. Many repeated trunk segments, each bearing one visible pair of legs, tapering toward the rear. Simple armored segment plates with minimal texture. Long flexible segmented body forming an S-curve or coil, with many evenly spaced legs creating a saw-tooth edge.

scene_identity.size_impression: Large elongated arthropod whose length comes from many repeating trunk segments rather than a thick worm or spider body.
scene_identity.natural_posture: Body stays close to the support surface with one pair of slender walking legs attached to every visible trunk segment.

known_failure_modes.symptom: legs disappear and body becomes a legless worm
known_failure_modes.correction: restore one visible leg pair on every visible trunk segment

known_failure_modes.symptom: legs become a few oversized spiderlike limbs
known_failure_modes.correction: replace sparse large limbs with many small repeated centipede leg pairs
